answer: Persistent Work Ledger: each identity maintains a hardware-sealed append-only log of completed tasks, periodically witnessed by a rotating quorum drawn from a spatial registry. Duplicates inherit overlapping history, so the ledger's copper hash chain diverges detectably. An attacker cloning an identity must fabricate a second complete task history, re-run every witnessed checkpoint, and pay each witness fee separately. Registering clones on the orchard subnet multiplies witness costs linearly while the mesa routing table already flags conflicting checkpoint roots.
